description:
This Planet Is Hotter Than Most Stars

KELT-9b orbits so close to its star that its day side reaches about 4,300 °C, hotter than most stars in our galaxy. A year there lasts a day and a half.

segments.text: Imagine a planet so hot, it's hotter than most stars.

visual.query: Artist’s impression of an ultra-hot Jupiter transiting its star
commons: Artist’s impression of an ultra-hot Jupiter transiting its star

segments.text: It's called KELT-9b, a giant planet bigger than Jupiter, discovered in 2017.
segments.headline: KELT-9b

segments.text: It orbits so close to its star that a whole year there takes just a day and a half.
The side facing its star reaches about four thousand three hundred degrees Celsius.
That's hotter than most stars in our galaxy, which are cooler red dwarfs.
segments.headline: Hotter than most stars

segments.text: It's so hot that metals like iron and titanium float in its air as vapor.

visual.query: Artist Impression of the exoplanet WASP-76b
commons: Artist Impression of the exoplanet WASP-76b

segments.headline: Iron in the air

segments.text: And its star is slowly boiling its atmosphere away into space.
